title: Zucchini, Basil and Ricotta Sauce
description: Peeled zucchini and soft ricotta make a pale green basil sauce for fish, chicken or pasta simmered directly in its sauce.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh zucchini
ingredients.note: Peel, weigh and cut into small cubes.

steps.title: Soften the zucchini
steps.text: Warm {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Add {zucchini} and {broth}, cover and simmer for 7–9 minutes until tender.

steps.title: Blend the basil base
steps.text: Blend the cooked zucchini, broth and {basil} in the deep jug until silky. Return to the skillet.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Set the reduction
steps.text: Measure the base and return it to the skillet. Aim for 1 1/4 cups. If needed, simmer briefly to reduce or add a splash of water to reach the mark.

steps.title: Whip in the ricotta
steps.text: Take the base off heat. Blend it with {ricotta} for 20–30 seconds until smooth and pale green.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon over steamed fish or poached chicken while warm. For a pasta meal, loosen the zucchini base with broth, simmer the pasta directly in it and fold in the ricotta at the end.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Chop the zucchini a day ahead. Add the basil on serving day for the freshest flavor. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Finished ricotta can become grainy in the freezer. For freezer prep, freeze the cooked zucchini base for up to 2 months, then blend in the fresh basil and ricotta after warming. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion over medium-low heat, whisking to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Whisk off heat until smooth. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. For dairy-free sauce, replace the ricotta with plain unsweetened dairy-free ricotta that blends smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 32 kcal, 1.9 g protein, 2.5 g total carbohydrate, 1.7 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 19 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
